front: Delegate-to-agent rule of thumb?
back: Delegate when success is checkable automatically and failure is cheap to undo (well-scoped, verifiable, reversible).

front: Name 3 good first tasks for a coding agent.
back: Tests for existing code, bug fixes with a failing repro, docs/dependency bumps/mechanical refactors.

front: Name 3 poor candidates for autonomous delegation.
back: Ambiguous requirements, cross-service architecture redesign, irreversible/production-affecting or security-critical work without review.

front: Anti-pattern: no definition of done. Mitigation?
back: Task template with objective acceptance criteria (tests, scans, scope limits).

front: Anti-pattern: one agent plans, codes, reviews and deploys. Mitigation?
back: Separate roles / separation of duties (planner, executor, reviewer).

front: Three parts of a well-defined agent task?
back: Inputs (goal, scope, constraints), outputs (draft PR, tests, log), success criteria (checkable).

front: How do you technically keep a planner from editing code?
back: Give it read/search tools only (tool restriction in the custom agent).

front: Why should a plan be structured?
back: So it can be validated (by people or automation) and compared with the final diff.

front: What does 'validate the plan' check?
back: Referenced files/tests exist, scope matches the task, criteria are met, risks and rollback noted.

front: How do you prevent action until a plan is approved?
back: A gate: approval label/comment/environment/re-assignment; executor write tools only enabled after approval.

front: Planning vs reasoning vs action?
back: Planning/reasoning are read-only analysis producing a plan; action mutates state (edit, commit, push, write tools).

front: Best natural checkpoint for human review of agent work on GitHub?
back: The (draft) pull request.

front: List inspectable artifacts from a cloud agent run.
back: Draft PR, co-authored signed commits, session logs, comments, Actions logs and scan results.

front: How to add human oversight without slowing delivery?
back: Review at PR boundary, CODEOWNERS/rulesets for sensitive paths, async steering, auto-allow low-risk read-only actions.

front: Why is 'approve every tool call' an anti-pattern?
back: It slows delivery without materially reducing risk; approvals should be risk-proportional.

front: Repo-wide instruction file path?
back: .github/copilot-instructions.md

front: Path-specific instruction files?
back: .github/instructions/*.instructions.md with applyTo frontmatter.

front: Where do repo-level custom agents live?
back: .github/agents/ (*.agent.md files). Org-level agents use the github-private repo.

front: What role does GitHub play for agents on this exam?
back: System of record and control plane: issues, branches, PRs, Actions, rulesets, session logs.

front: Strong vs weak success criteria?
back: Strong: 'failing test added and passing, suite green, no new CodeQL alerts, only src/billing changed'. Weak: 'make it work'.
